function: Distributed beamforming and power control by a GNN: each BS outputs its data beamformer (and pilot beamformer) vector to minimize the worst-link decoding error probability in mURLLC (pp. 4-6).
system: Downlink interference network of K=20 BS-UE links; BS with Nt=4 antennas, single-antenna UE; no RIS; 2.4 GHz, 5 MHz, 1 ms frames (pp. 4, 9-10).
method: GNN (G4U, PG4U) with feedforward kernels, trained offline and centrally without labels (unsupervised) by Adam on a Gaussian Q-function-based loss; distributed inference by pilot aggregation (pp. 5, 8-9).
data_channel: Simulated layouts: 2x10^4 training, 5x10^4 testing, K=20 links in 500 m square; path loss of [39] (ITU-R P.1411), 3 dB shadowing, Gauss-Markov fading rho=0.99 (pp. 4, 9, 14).
test_conditions: Trained at K=20 links, 80 links/km2, rho=0.99, 1 ms frames; trained models tested at K=10-35, density ratio 0.5-2 and rho 0-1; frame duration 0.2-2 ms (pp. 9-12).
baselines: Non-learned: WMMSE (10 iterations, no overhead) and equal power allocation; learned: existing GNN [28] with overhead, and GNN* ignoring overhead (p. 9).
metrics: QoS outage probability Pr(eps_max > 1e-5), average utility, versus number of links, link density, frame duration, channel correlation (pp. 10-12).
complexity: Computation delay Tc=(2N+1)tc for GNN, 3tc for G4U, 0 for PG4U, with tc=100 us assumed (not measured); signaling overhead also modeled (pp. 6-9).
q1_support: p. 9: "by using the channel model (2) to capture the temporal correlation". Custom AR(1) small-scale fading (Eq. 2, p. 4); only the path loss follows ITU-R P.1411 [39] (pp. 9, 14); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 11: "We now test the scalability of the trained GNN models in terms of the QoS outage probability". Training uses K = 20 links (p. 9); Fig. 6(a) tests K = 10-35 and Fig. 6(b) 0.5-2 times the training link density.
q3_support: p. 9: "WMMSE [26]: This is the conventional state-of-the-art optimization-based algorithm"; p. 9: "GNN* [28]: We ignore the signaling overhead and computation delay". Both compared on average utility and QoS outage probability (Figs. 5-8); the GNN of [28] is an earlier learned method.
q4_support: p. 7: "the computation delay of G4U is given by" Tc = 3tc. Counts FNN executions (3 for G4U, 2N+1 for GNN, p. 6) at an assumed 100 us each (p. 9); no FLOPs, parameters or measured runtime.
q5_support: p. 3: "The codes to reproduce the simulation results are available on https://github.com/Yifan-Gu-SZU/G4U-GNN-for-mURLLC".
notes: Title on p. 1 matches the DOI. Area 3: distributed beamforming and power control with GNNs, BSs have Nt=4 antennas so the system check passes. q1 is 0: the small-scale fading is custom and only the path loss follows ITU-R P.1411 [39] (p. 9); reviewer may confirm. q4 is 1 on the modeled computation delay (number of FNN executions times an assumed 100 us, pp. 6-9), which is not signaling overhead alone, but it is not FLOPs, parameters or measured runtime; reviewer to confirm. q3: the learned baseline is the earlier GNN of [28], the non-learned ones are WMMSE and equal power allocation.
